title: French Toast
description: Classic American French toast with crisp buttery edges and a soft vanilla-custard center, ready for maple syrup and fresh fruit.
ingredients: Maple syrup and berries, for serving
instructions: Set the bread on a rack for 10 minutes so the surface dries slightly and can absorb custard without becoming fragile.
Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, sugar, and salt in a wide shallow dish until completely blended.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium-low heat so the custard can cook through before the bread browns too deeply.
Melt a small portion of the butter and spread it across the cooking surface.
Dip two bread slices in the custard, turning once and allowing each side to absorb the mixture for about 15 seconds.
Lift the bread and let excess custard drip back into the dish before placing it in the skillet.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the underside is evenly golden and the edges begin to look set.
Flip carefully and cook the second side for another 3 minutes, adjusting the heat if the butter browns too quickly.
Repeat with the remaining bread and butter, keeping finished slices warm in a low oven if needed.
Serve immediately with maple syrup, berries, and a light dusting of cinnamon or powdered sugar.
tips: Use day-old thick bread for the best custard absorption.
Keep the heat moderate so the center cooks fully.
Whisk the custard again between batches because cinnamon can settle.
commonMistakes: Soaking thin fresh bread too long can make it fall apart.
High heat browns the exterior before the egg mixture sets.
Crowding the pan makes flipping difficult.
substitutions: Use Texas toast instead of brioche.
Use half-and-half for a richer custard.
Use dairy-free milk and plant-based butter if preferred.
storage: Refrigerate cooled slices for up to 3 days.
Reheat in a toaster oven or skillet for crisp edges.
Freeze separated by parchment for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Cinnamon French Toast
description: Warm cinnamon-spiced French toast with caramelized buttery edges and a tender custard center.
ingredients: 8 thick slices brioche or Texas toast
instructions: Arrange the bread in a single layer for several minutes to dry the surfaces slightly.
Whisk eggs and milk until no streaks of egg white remain.
Whisk in cinnamon, vanilla, brown sugar, and salt until the sugar begins to dissolve.
Preheat a wide skillet over medium-low heat and melt enough butter to lightly coat it.
Dip each bread slice into the cinnamon custard and turn to coat both sides evenly.
Allow excess custard to drip away so it does not pool around the bread in the skillet.
Cook in batches for about 3 minutes on the first side until deep golden brown.
Flip and cook the second side until browned and the center feels softly set rather than wet.
Add fresh butter between batches and stir the custard before each dip to redistribute the cinnamon.
Serve hot with maple syrup and an optional extra pinch of cinnamon.
tips: Stir the custard often so cinnamon stays evenly distributed.
Thick bread gives a creamy center without becoming soggy.
Use medium-low heat for even browning.
commonMistakes: Too much cinnamon can clump on the surface.
Over-soaking soft bread makes it fragile.
Burning the butter creates bitter dark spots.
substitutions: Use challah in place of brioche.
Use light brown or granulated sugar.
Add a pinch of nutmeg for extra warmth.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
Reheat in a skillet or toaster oven.
Freeze cooked slices for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Breakfast Burritos
description: Crisp breakfast burritos packed with fluffy eggs, savory ham, cheese, and fresh tomato for a filling make-ahead breakfast.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack or mozzarella
instructions: Warm the tortillas briefly so they are flexible and less likely to crack when rolled.
Whisk eggs with sour cream, salt, and pepper until smooth and slightly aerated.
Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and add the egg mixture.
Cook slowly, folding with a spatula until the eggs form soft moist curds, then remove them from the heat.
Lay the tortillas flat and divide the scrambled eggs across the lower third of each one.
Top evenly with ham, shredded cheese, and diced tomato while leaving a clear border around the filling.
Fold the sides inward, then roll each tortilla tightly from the bottom to form a sealed burrito.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a clean skillet over medium heat and place burritos seam-side down.
Cook and turn until each side is crisp and golden and the cheese inside has melted.
Rest for 2 minutes before slicing or wrapping for later serving.
tips: Keep scrambled eggs slightly soft because they cook again in the burrito.
Do not overfill the tortillas.
Start crisping seam-side down to seal the wrap.
commonMistakes: Cold tortillas tear during rolling.
Watery fillings make burritos soggy.
Overcooked eggs become rubbery after reheating.
substitutions: Use cooked bacon or breakfast sausage instead of ham.
Use cheddar instead of Monterey Jack.
Omit tomato when freezing.
storage: Refrigerate wrapped burritos for up to 3 days.
Freeze individually for up to 1 month.
Reheat until the center is steaming hot.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Breakfast Casserole
description: A crowd-friendly American breakfast casserole layered with eggs, bacon, vegetables, and melted cheddar.
ingredients: 2 cups frozen diced hash browns, thawed
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9-by-13-inch baking dish thoroughly.
Cook the onion and bell pepper in a skillet until softened and any excess moisture has evaporated.
Spread the thawed hash browns evenly across the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Scatter the cooked vegetables and chopped bacon over the potatoes in an even layer.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper until fully combined and slightly frothy.
Pour the egg mixture slowly over the casserole so it settles between the fillings.
Sprinkle the cheddar evenly over the surface without pressing it into the eggs.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the edges are puffed and the center is just set.
Rest the casserole for 10 minutes so the egg structure firms enough for clean slices.
Cut into squares and serve warm with hot sauce or fresh herbs if desired.
tips: Thaw potatoes to prevent excess water.
Cook watery vegetables before assembling.
Remove from the oven as soon as the center sets.
commonMistakes: Frozen wet potatoes can make the casserole watery.
Overbaking makes eggs rubbery.
Cutting immediately causes messy portions.
substitutions: Use cooked sausage instead of bacon.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Add spinach after wilting it dry.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 4 days.
Reheat individual portions gently.
Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Sausage Breakfast Casserole
description: Savory sausage breakfast casserole with bread, eggs, milk, and cheddar baked until golden and set.
instructions: Butter a 9-by-13-inch baking dish and spread the bread cubes evenly over the bottom.
Brown the breakfast sausage in a skillet, breaking it into small pieces as it cooks.
Drain excess rendered fat and scatter the cooked sausage evenly over the bread.
Whisk eggs, milk, dry mustard, salt, and pepper until completely blended.
Pour the custard slowly over the bread and sausage, pressing the bread lightly so it begins absorbing liquid.
Scatter the shredded cheddar evenly over the top and cover the dish.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, so the bread absorbs the seasoned egg mixture.
Heat the oven to 350°F and let the chilled casserole stand at room temperature while the oven heats.
Bake uncovered for 45 to 50 minutes until golden and fully set in the center.
Rest for 10 minutes, garnish with green onions, and cut into squares for serving.
tips: Day-old bread absorbs custard without turning mushy.
Drain sausage well before layering.
An overnight rest makes morning preparation easier.
commonMistakes: Fresh soft bread can collapse into the custard.
Greasy sausage can make the casserole heavy.
Underbaking leaves liquid egg in the center.
substitutions: Use turkey breakfast sausage.
Use pepper Jack for more heat.
Add sautéed bell peppers or mushrooms.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Reheat covered at 325°F or in individual portions.
Freeze baked portions for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Eggs Benedict
description: Classic Eggs Benedict with toasted English muffins, Canadian bacon, poached eggs, and silky lemon hollandaise.
instructions: Toast the English muffin halves until golden and keep them warm while preparing the remaining components.
Warm the Canadian bacon in a skillet until lightly browned on both sides, then place one slice on each muffin half.
Bring a wide saucepan of water to a bare simmer and add the vinegar; avoid a rolling boil.
Crack each egg into a small cup, slide it gently into the water, and poach until the white is set but the yolk remains soft.
Meanwhile, place egg yolks and lemon juice in a blender and blend briefly until smooth.
With the blender running on low, drizzle in the warm melted butter very slowly until a thick glossy hollandaise forms.
Season the hollandaise with salt and cayenne, thinning with a teaspoon of warm water if necessary.
Lift the poached eggs with a slotted spoon and blot the bottoms briefly on a clean towel.
Set one poached egg over each Canadian-bacon-topped muffin half and spoon warm hollandaise generously over the top.
Garnish with chives and cayenne and serve immediately while the eggs and sauce are warm.
tips: Keep poaching water at a gentle simmer.
Drizzle butter slowly to keep hollandaise emulsified.
Prepare all components before poaching the eggs.
commonMistakes: Boiling water tears delicate egg whites.
Adding butter too quickly can split hollandaise.
Letting assembled Benedict sit too long cools the sauce.
substitutions: Use ham or crisp bacon instead of Canadian bacon.
Use toasted sourdough rounds instead of English muffins.
Add spinach for an Eggs Florentine-style variation.
storage: Poached eggs are best served immediately.
Refrigerate leftover cooked components separately for up to 2 days.
Hollandaise should be made fresh for best texture.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Hash Browns
description: Crispy skillet hash browns with deeply golden edges and tender shredded potato centers.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil or bacon fat
instructions: Peel the russet potatoes and grate them on the large holes of a box grater.
Gather the shreds in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze firmly until as much moisture as possible is removed.
Transfer the dry potatoes to a bowl and toss with onion powder while keeping the shreds loose.
Preheat a 10-inch cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium heat and add half the oil and half the butter.
Spread half the potatoes into an even layer about one-third inch thick without packing them tightly.
Cook undisturbed for about 5 to 6 minutes so a crisp golden crust can develop.
Season the top with salt and pepper, then flip the hash browns in sections or as one round.
Add a little more oil and butter around the edges and cook the second side until crisp and deeply golden.
Transfer to a rack or warm plate and repeat with the remaining potatoes and fat.
Season immediately and serve hot while the exterior is at its crispiest.
tips: Removing moisture is the key to crisp hash browns.
Do not stir while the crust is forming.
Keep the potato layer relatively thin.
commonMistakes: Wet potatoes steam instead of crisping.
Flipping too early breaks the crust.
Overcrowding creates a soft center.
substitutions: Use bacon fat for a smoky flavor.
Add a small amount of grated onion, squeezed dry.
Use clarified butter for higher-heat cooking.
storage: Refrigerate cooked hash browns for up to 3 days.
Reheat in a skillet or air fryer.
Freeze cooked portions for up to 1 month.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Home Fries
description: Diner-style home fries with crisp-edged potatoes, sweet onion, bell pepper, and savory breakfast seasoning.
ingredients: 2 lb russet potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
instructions: Place the diced potatoes in salted water, bring to a gentle boil, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until barely tender at the edges.
Drain thoroughly and let the potatoes steam-dry for several minutes so their surfaces are no longer wet.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and add the avocado oil.
Add the potatoes in a single layer and leave them undisturbed for several minutes to develop a brown crust.
Turn the potatoes and continue cooking until multiple sides are golden and crisp.
Push the potatoes toward the edges, add butter to the center, and add the onion and bell pepper.
Cook the vegetables until softened and lightly browned, then fold them through the potatoes.
Season with paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper and toss until the spices coat everything evenly.
Cook for another 2 to 3 minutes until the potatoes are fully tender inside and crisp outside.
Finish with parsley, taste for seasoning, and serve immediately with eggs or other breakfast favorites.
tips: Parboil only until the potato edges soften.
Steam-dry before frying.
Use a wide skillet so potatoes can brown in one layer.
commonMistakes: Crowding the skillet causes steaming.
Moving potatoes constantly prevents browning.
Overboiling makes the cubes fall apart.
substitutions: Use Yukon Gold potatoes for a creamier center.
Use green bell pepper instead of red.
Cook in bacon fat instead of avocado oil.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Reheat uncovered in a hot skillet.
Freeze for up to 1 month, though freshly cooked texture is best.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Breakfast Tacos
description: Easy breakfast tacos filled with fluffy scrambled eggs, chorizo, cheese, avocado, and fresh salsa.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese
Fresh cilantro and hot sauce, for serving
instructions: Cook the chorizo in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it into small crumbles until browned and fully cooked.
Transfer the cooked chorizo to a plate and keep it warm while leaving only a light coating of fat in the skillet.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a low gas flame until flexible and lightly toasted.
Stack the warm tortillas in a clean towel so they remain soft while the eggs cook.
Whisk the eggs with milk and salt until the mixture is uniform and slightly frothy.
Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and pour in the eggs.
Cook slowly, sweeping a spatula through the pan to form soft curds, and remove from heat while the eggs still look slightly moist.
Divide the eggs among the warm tortillas and immediately sprinkle each portion with cheese so it begins to melt.
Top with chorizo, avocado, pico de gallo, cilantro, and hot sauce according to taste.
Fold the tacos gently and serve immediately while the tortillas are warm and the eggs are tender.
tips: Warm tortillas before filling so they do not crack.
Remove scrambled eggs while slightly moist.
Offer toppings separately when serving a group.
commonMistakes: Overcooked eggs make the filling dry.
Cold tortillas split when folded.
Overfilling makes tacos difficult to eat.
substitutions: Use bacon instead of chorizo.
Use corn tortillas for a gluten-free option.
Use black beans in place of meat.
storage: Store cooked fillings separately for up to 3 days.
Reheat eggs gently and tortillas separately.
Add avocado and fresh salsa only when serving.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
